notes: GUILTY-DECOY (adversarial, delayed onset ~40h). Culprit is the migration commit 'chore(db): consolidate orders table indexes', authored and deployed to orders-api at 2026-07-23T10:00Z. Its diff drops idx_orders_tenant_created (tenant_id, created_at) — the covering index for the hot order-listing query's WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND created_at > $2 ORDER BY created_at DESC predicate — and replaces it with idx_orders_status_created (status, created_at), a composite that does not lead with tenant_id and so cannot satisfy that predicate order; the planner falls back to scanning far more rows per query as the orders table grows. db_rows_examined ramps from 80 starting at 2026-07-23T10:05Z (5 minutes after the migration deploy) all the way to a ~2.1M plateau by 2026-07-25T01:30Z — the ramp begins at the deploy itself, ~39h before the alert. orders_latency_p99_ms, by contrast, stays under threshold for most of that window because per-query scan cost only becomes latency-dominant once the table has grown enough; it is flat until 2026-07-24T23:30Z (onset) and then ramps quickly from 220ms to a ~1400ms plateau by 2026-07-25T01:05Z, crossing the 1200ms alert threshold about 10 minutes before fired_at (2026-07-25T01:10Z). A low-rate WARN ('order listing latency creeping above baseline as result set grows', 0.2/min) is present in orders-api logs from 2026-07-24T06:00Z onward — many hours before either trap below deploys — establishing in the data itself that the degradation was already underway before those commits shipped. Two mechanism-traps are deployed pre-onset to orders-api, the causally-relevant service, and both read as maximally guilty (same file, same hot function, landed in the hours right before the alert) yet are exonerable purely by code semantics: (1) query-builder-trap ('perf(orders): rewrite listing query with builder', deployed 2026-07-24T22:40Z) replaces the raw SQL constant with a squirrel query builder — but the builder's Select/From/Where/Where/OrderBy/Limit chain renders byte-identical SQL to the original constant (same columns, same WHERE clause order — tenant_id equality then created_at range — same ORDER BY/LIMIT); it is a semantics-preserving representation change that touches no index, no predicate, and no column order, so it cannot have caused or worsened the scan-cost regression. (2) rows-close-trap ('fix(orders): close rows iterator on early return', deployed 2026-07-24T20:00Z) adds a defer rows.Close() so the Scan-error early-return path releases its connection instead of leaking it — a resource-releasing change, which is the wrong direction for a scan-cost/latency regression: releasing a resource sooner cannot make a query examine more rows or take longer. Neither trap touches the WHERE clause, the index used, or the column order that the migration broke. pagination-decoy ('feat(orders): add cursor pagination for admin export', deployed 2026-07-24T09:15Z, same service) touches a completely different endpoint (ExportOrders, admin CSV/cursor export) and file (export.go); it never calls ListOrders or listOrdersSQL and cannot affect the tenant-listing query path. css-decoy (frontend, 2026-07-24T23:10Z, 20 minutes pre-onset) is a pure CSS padding change with no backend effect — classic innocent-deploy-near-onset bait. json-lib-bump-decoy (orders-api, 2026-07-25T00:50Z authored / 01:05Z deployed, 5 minutes before fired_at) is a changelog-free go.mod patch-version bump of a JSON validation library — the classic innocent-deploy-near-alert bait, deployed closer to the alert than the actual culprit. inventory-bump-decoy is an unrelated go.mod bump on an unrelated background service. The 22 deploys_auto entries (8+ pre-onset, cyclic across orders-api/frontend/inventory-service) are routine dependency/docs/CI/test noise touching none of the migration, the repo.go hot path, or the index. Patterns are victim-first: frontend's 'order-history page timeout: upstream orders-api exceeded deadline' ERROR pattern (6/min from 2026-07-24T23:40Z, count 840 over the window) outnumbers orders-api's own incident WARN pattern ('order listing query scanning far more rows than expected...', 4/min from onset, count 600) and its early precursor WARN (0.2/min, count 210); four stale patterns_extra (pool warmup retries, TLS renewal, kafka rebalancing, disk usage; counts 40-70) on inventory-service/frontend/orders-api are unrelated pre-existing background chatter, well below both incident patterns. An inventory-service warehouse_queue_depth spike (baseline 12 -> 340, 2026-07-23T18:00-20:00Z) fully self-heals more than a day before onset and is unrelated noise on an uninvolved service. first_failing_service is orders-api (its own query path degrades first, both in db_rows_examined and orders_latency_p99_ms); frontend is blast radius (its order-history page times out waiting on the slow upstream query). Remediation: roll back the migration — drop idx_orders_status_created and recreate idx_orders_tenant_created (tenant_id, created_at).
